Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and great demo. Quick answers below: 

- PII scope: Customer names, account numbers, and transaction metadata are in-scope. No SSNs or full payment card numbers are expected to be sent to the service.
- Retention: We have a default 30-day retention requirement for any logs that contain PII; for analytics/embeddings we prefer 90 days but can negotiate.
- Residency: We require data at-rest to remain in us-east-1 for production workloads.

Support access question: our security team will need the details of your break-glass workflow and the audit trail for any support session that elevates privileges or downloads customer data. Can you attach the support-access doc you mentioned?

I'm looping in procurement (procurement@fintrust.com) to start the contracting timeline — they're primarily interested in SLA/credits and onboarding milestones.

Appreciate the details, Alex — that's very helpful. 

I've attached the two docs we discussed: SOC2_summary.pdf and Redwood_Support_Access_Doc.pdf. High level from the support-access doc: 

- Default support access is strictly role-based and time-limited. Support engineers can request an elevated session which requires a justification, approver (on-call manager), and explicit scope (read-only vs read-write).
- Break-glass: used only for production incidents with business impact. Break-glass requires two approvers and is time-limited; it generates an automatic ticket and an immediate audit log entry.
- Audit logging: all support sessions are recorded (session metadata + command transcript); any download of customer data is flagged and requires an immediate post-incident review.
- RBAC: we expose service roles (admin, ops_read, ops_write, support_read) and allow customers to map those to their own SSO groups. We support least-privilege by default — customers can request narrower roles (e.g., no subset of ops_write).

Action items: 
- Alex/procurement: confirm the retention window you want Redwood to enforce (30 vs 90 days) and whether you need a contract clause for data residency in us-east-1.
- Security: Rishi/Monica, can you confirm whether the break-glass two-approver requirement is sufficient for FinTrust, or do they require an out-of-band approval?
- Scheduling: Alex, Marissa proposes Wed 10:00-10:30 PST (Wed 15:00-15:30 EST). Does that work?

Thanks — I'll hold the slot tentatively.
